newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee futures end down but at day's peak.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee futures end down but at day's peak.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures regained some lost ground in the afternoon to end Friday with pared losses helped by late arbitrage buying against New York.
Traders said further industry buying on the dips also helped values.
But conditions remained dull and thin with major players still reluctant to dabble after the recent spate of sharp volatility.
Benchmark May rebounded from the session low of $1,686 a tonne to end the day near the peak at $1,686, just $8 down.
The market had earlier bucked pre-opening calls of $100-$200 lower and managed to come in just $60-$70 down.
Volume was 5,564 lots. May/May arbitrage with New York stood at 109.03 cents in late London trading.
Traders said the robusta market was probably heading for a pause, consolidating its recent gains after a new rally to $1,825 a tonne basis May, a peak not seen since last June.
Friday's slide was also halted by a dearth of sellers notably from Asia on the sharply lower call.
"We have done better than it was technically due this morning and that's purely because you're not seeing the same origin selling coming out from the Far East," said one.
Technically, May faces strong support at the $1,600-$1,630 chart gap while the upside goal is pegged at a chart gap of between $1,702 and $1,728, Thursday's high and Wedneday's low respectively.
New York's arabica futures rebounded to reach a high of 190.50 cents a lb in morning U.S. trading after falling to Thursday's low of 181. It had closed the day at 182.25.
